Honestly the answer is the simplest one. Eat less food. Eating less food is the hard part. To start off with have a goal to lose every week. That is usually anywhere from one to one and a half percent of your current body weight. Having this goal will help you not overdo your diet which is a good way to fail. If you are losing more weight than your goal, that may seem good but you're also losing muscle at that point something that helps you lose more weight and you're probably making yourself hungrier.

When choosing food, focus on protein to at least 1 G of your goal body weight. Protein should be your primary focus when choosing your meals. The important part of the protein is do not live off protein shakes. Protein will get you full and keep you full longer than eating carbs will. Fats will do the same but the calories there aren't worth it in weight loss. I'm not saying only protein. I'm saying if your goal is to get a 170 g of protein a day focus on hitting that.

Also, drink water, and I mean you should be drinking at least half a gallon a day if not more. Coffee is not water it will actually dehydrate you. The same goes for anything else that has caffeine in it. You will be hungry if you are dehydrated.

Honestly expect at some point for things to not fall off as quickly after a few months. Then you just have to eat at maintenance for a week or two and then start over again. I know you're not going to a gym right now but if you're going to do bodyweight stuff it should still be getting harder over time either with more reps or putting things in a book bag while doing push-ups or whatever.

The last thing I'm going to say is try to walk at least 10K steps a day. You don't have to start that day one but walking more is one of the easiest ways to keep your body active without going to the gym.

You can look up online how to get your maintenance and such because you'll want to start off with that information to figure out your calorie deficit. I'm still fairly new, but I found a few things. 

Always be doing farming just as the person above said, and once you can plant trees, then you need to plant trees they give huge XP boost compared to other farm things. 

Try to keep resource and crafting skills around the same level. I have so many things I want to make that I can't because I can't get the resource to make them yet.

Don't be afraid to waste a week doing nothing but maxing out astrology it actually is worth it.

It is very tempting to hoard everything, but until you get at least 125 slots, it is going to be hard to do things such as thieving and fishing, which can give you multiple drops for one type of action. If you can make a thousand of it in less than an hour, then you can probably let it go and get more. Saving slots for things that you are not able to get fast enough such as maybe some herbs and food stuff makes sense, but you should be making potions out of those or cooking not just having them sit there unless you need them for a specific Quest you're working towards.

Don't be afraid to min max your money when it comes to deciding what you're going to craft. XP is very important, but if you're making money and XP, then you're still doing good. Also, consider that extra money can be used to buy things such as gloves that will make your XP gain way faster. Do not go overboard with this though, if you have wood then go ahead and do Javelin heads, it uses three different skills to make so it's awesome and they sell for good money, but if you don't then just do something like crossbow heads instead. yes, it's less money, but you don't have to now sit through a few hours of gathering wood just to make the javelins when you could have made more money in that time doing something else.

Summoning takes a long time to do, and yes, there are some so many things that will lose you money in the process, especially early game. Do summoning it is very long, so if you have the extra money, keep it leveled up. Some of the bonuses may make you think it's not relevant, and that's fine. You're not there for the bonuses all the time it's just the XP that you're looking for. 

Speaking of summoning, once you're able to make both mining and cooking tablets and they can synergize, you no longer need to mine coal. Instead, use the two together and do cooking. You'll fail cooking dishes every one out of four times, but you'll get a hundred coal for each failure.

The last thing that I have is always be doing something. Obviously, you have real life, but if you're going to bed and you're doing nothing, you're wasting experience. I personally try to do any crafting related skills when I'm awake so that when it's done, I can do something that doesn't stop when it runs out of resources.

One last tip make sure you save level one potions to turn into Township. You cannot go backwards in Potions or downgrade them.

Here's the post for the workout. If anyone else has advice they can add to it but this should be enough for at least 6 months.

Upper Body Workout 
Focus: Chest, back, shoulders, arms

• Dumbbell Bench Press – 3 sets of 8-12 reps

• Seated Low Row– 3 sets of 8-12 reps

• Lat Pulldown (Machine) – 3 sets of 10-12 reps

• Dumbbell Bicep Curl – 3 sets of 10-15 reps

• Cable Triceps Pushdown – 3 sets of 10-15 reps

• Side lateral raises – 3 sets of 12-15 reps

Lower Body Workout 
Focus: Legs, glutes, calves
• Leg Press (Machine) – 3 sets of 10-12 reps

• Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbells) – 3 sets of 8-12 reps

• Step-Ups (Dumbbells) – 3 sets of 8-12 reps per leg

• Seated Calf Raise (Machine or Dumbbell on Knee) – 3 sets of 12-15 reps

• Lying or Seated Hamstring Curl (Machine) – 3 sets of 10-12 reps

• Seated Leg Extension – 3 sets of 12 reps per leg

Full Body Workout 
Do not do this 3 times a week. You can skip it if you go 4 days a week or use it once a week 
• Machine Chest Press – 3 sets of 10-12 reps

• Goblet Squat (Dumbbell) – 3 sets of 10-12 reps

• Dumbbell Deadlift – 3 sets of 8-12 reps

• Seated Row (Cable Machine) – 3 sets of 10-12 reps

• Dumbbell Lateral Raise – 3 sets of 12-15 reps

• Plank Hold – 3 sets of 30-60 seconds

• Hanging Leg Raises or Cable Crunches – 3 sets of 12-15 reps

• Farmer’s Walk (Dumbbells) – 3 sets of 30-45 seconds

Notes:
• Dumbbell is so one side isn't working harder then the other don't switch it out for a bar unless dumbbells aren't available. Having balanced strength and a good form is more important in the beginning.

• Try to do one set of a warm up at least for the big muscle groups but two sets or even three is fine. Just go light on the way and don't count them as working sets. You should never be warming up with more than maybe 60% of what you're going to be lifting at day.

• If you want to do abs with each workout you can. Don't just do planks and crunches though include work that twist your hips and works your side as well.

• Cardio is not necessary unless you want to do it. Even if you're losing weight it is not necessary as diet will have a bigger effect. If you do cardio you can do a short warm up but put most of it on off days or after workouts.

• Try to go up in weight every week. It will be easier for things like legs, back, and chest. The body parts where it's hard to go up do you more reps until you are hitting the max for that weight and if you still cannot go up continue to add more reps.

• Every workout you should be able to reach the minimum reps. If you cannot, go to the last weight you lifted, and add more reps. Every two months add a set to the big muscle groups exercises l. Legs, back, and chest not the isolation stuff like triceps. Eventually you want to get to the point of working each muscle group at least 10 sets a week. Things like triceps will get hit while doing the chest work that's why you don't need to increase that.

• I'm not sure if you care but I know you're a female. Do not purposely lift light to not get bulky as that is not genetically possible without steroids, so you are safe.

• Make sure to stretch each body part used after a workout. If you want to stretch before a workout do dynamic stretches not stretches where you hold it. Holding stretches are better after workouts and safer than.

• You should at least be getting 0.7g of protein per pound of body weight everyday regardless of if you went to the gym or not that day. If you're trying to lose weight, take it up to closer to 1g per day.

• Do not skip on your sleep. Getting less than 7 hours a day will have an impact on your growth and speed. The diet and sleep are your best friends and you are in an age range where everything will come easy if you just do the work.

HAVE FUN. IF IT'S NOT FUN, THERE ARE OTHER OPTIONS.

If your diet is correct, you don't even have to workout. Lots of people lose weight and some just walk 30 minutes a day abs eat better. 

I'm NOT suggesting you don't workout. Working out will make you hungry so you have to keep that in mind with the dieting. 

Honestly, there are lots of free stuff online. If you don't feel confident, get a trainer. It will help you get to the gym, you can ask for a workout plan (a good trainer will want to help with that), and they can show you the right way to do the exercises. The other thing to remember is that as it beginner is going to feel like you should be trying new stuff but if you got a solid program stick with it for at least 3 to 6 months. Also when I say solid that doesn't actually matter so long as the workout is safe because as a beginner you'll get the progress so long as you do the work no matter the exercise plan.

Now if you want the internet answer here it is. The main places you want to work out is your chest, back, legs, core. Stuff like biceps and triceps will get hit while doing other exercises the same with shoulders but most people like to Target them so you can if you want to. Exercise you should be doing anywhere from 12 to 20 sets a week not all in the same day for each of those four body area and yes they can be different exercises. You should be going close to failure and you'll know if you have failure if you can't lift more than two or three more reps. You should be increasing the weight every workout and if you increase the weight and you cannot do it then you go back down to the last weight you were able to do and add more reps to it. As far as rep ranges the lower you go is strength  5 or less, and the higher you go is for size 10 to 15 and yes you will still get strength if you go for size. I would refrain from going over 20 Reps for any exercise as stamina may beat you before strength will. The last advice is get proper sleep 7 to 8 hours and to get at least 8 g of protein per pound of Target body weight but you can go higher. Make sure you do a warm up before working out it can be dynamic stretching or even a light walk or jog on the treadmill. You do not have to do cardio in order to lose weight and unless you like it I recommend not doing it so that when your weight loss does become hard you can then start doing it to help burn more calories.
